theory.intro: An unknown angle at a point is found by matching the diagram to an angle total or an equality, then stating the reason.

workedExamples.solution_text:
Angles on a straight line add to $180^{\circ}$.

$\begin{aligned}55^{\circ}+60^{\circ}+x&=180^{\circ}\\115^{\circ}+x&=180^{\circ}\\x&=65^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

Angles in a right angle add to $90^{\circ}$.

$\begin{aligned}24^{\circ}+36^{\circ}+x&=90^{\circ}\\60^{\circ}+x&=90^{\circ}\\x&=30^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

Angles at a point add to $360^{\circ}$.

$\begin{aligned}x+65^{\circ}+85^{\circ}&=360^{\circ}\\x+150^{\circ}&=360^{\circ}\\x&=210^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

Angles at a point add to $360^{\circ}$.

$\begin{aligned}b+2b+3b+210&=360\\6b+210&=360\\6b&=150\\b&=25\end{aligned}$

The three unknown angles are $25^{\circ}$, $50^{\circ}$ and $75^{\circ}$.

The whole upper angle is $32^{\circ}+54^{\circ}=86^{\circ}$.

Vertically opposite angles are equal, so $x=86^{\circ}$.
